report.incidentSummary: Starting around 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC) on 2026-10-07, assistant replies began taking 20-25 seconds and approximately 6% of conversations failed with generic 'Something went wrong' fallback messages. Investigation established that the external LLM provider began enforcing an active token quota rate limit of 200,000 tokens per minute at 05:50:04 UTC, returning HTTP 429 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000'. The assistant-orchestrator's retry policy executed up to 3 sequential retries with 2 to 7 second backoffs upon receiving 429 responses, inflating overall p95 conversation latency from ~6.5 s to ~25 s and exhausting retries for ~6% of queries.
report.rootCauseStatement: Upstream rate limiting and quota enforcement by external llm-provider (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000') starting at 05:50:04 UTC, compounded by assistant-orchestrator executing up to three sequential backoff retries without client-side token-bucket rate limiting or circuit breaking, which inflated conversation latency to 20-25 seconds and resulted in fallback errors upon retry exhaustion.

hypotheses.cause: External llm-provider strictly enforced an active rate limit of 200,000 tokens per minute against the assistant API key starting at 05:50:04 UTC. Because assistant-orchestrator's token demand hovered near or above this threshold, requests received sustained HTTP 429 responses, triggering repeated sequential retries that inflated conversational latency to 20-25 seconds and caused fallback errors when all 3 attempts failed.
hypotheses.rationale: Logs directly capture HTTP 429 responses with message 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000' beginning at 05:50:04 UTC. Rate_limited_count rose from 0 to 33-79/min while chat traffic remained steady (~22 req/s), ruling out a traffic surge. All 151 orchestrator error logs during the window were HTTP 429 retry exhaustion failures.

hypotheses.cause: assistant-orchestrator lacks client-side adaptive rate limiting, token-bucket smoothing, or circuit breaking, executing up to 3 sequential retries with 2-7 s backoffs when receiving HTTP 429 from llm-provider, converting upstream rate limiting into 20-25 s conversation delays and fallback errors.
hypotheses.rationale: This mechanism explains the severe latency amplification (p95 jumping from 6.5s to 25s) and user-facing fallback errors, but acts reactively to the upstream 429 status codes rather than originating the rate limit.

hypotheses.cause: The knowledge index rebuild (CHG-48222) started at 05:30 UTC degraded retrieval performance or shared llm-provider credentials, causing delays and errors in assistant-orchestrator.
hypotheses.rationale: knowledge-index p95 latency only increased by ~280 ms (to ~360 ms) due to cache warming, and error rate remained at 0.10% with zero ingest errors. assistant-orchestrator's knowledge-index retrieval timeout is 800 ms with 0 retries, which cannot account for 20+ second delays or HTTP 429 responses from llm-provider.

assistant-orchestrator llm_latency_p95_ms rose from ~5.0-5.5 seconds before 05:50 UTC to 11.3 seconds at 05:50 UTC and 22.2-23.3 seconds from 05:55 UTC onwards.

Starting at 05:50:04.497 UTC, assistant-orchestrator logged repeated HTTP 429 Too Many Requests errors from llm-provider with message 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000', triggering multi-second retry backoffs across 3 attempts.
All 151 ERROR logs in assistant-orchestrator between 05:00 and 07:30 UTC have status 429 and message template 'conversation <id> failed: llm-provider 429 after 3 attempts; returned fallback message'.
assistant-orchestrator conversation error_rate rose from baseline ~0.50% to 5.82%-6.11% starting at 05:55 UTC.
The first recorded conversation failure error occurred at 2026-10-07T05:52:02.886 UTC for model lumen-large-2026-08.

assistant-orchestrator llm_tokens_per_min was 253k-268k tokens/min between 05:00 and 05:25 UTC, 211k-223k between 05:30 and 05:45 UTC, 185.5k at 05:50 UTC, and 165k-176k thereafter.

inferences.statement: The 20+ second conversation latency is caused by cumulative retry backoff delays (up to 3 attempts with 2 to 7 s pauses) following HTTP 429 rate limit responses from llm-provider, rather than internal document retrieval, compliance checks, or context retrieval.
Chat traffic volume did not trigger the throttling, as request rate was flat to declining (~22 req/s) at 05:50 UTC.

The knowledge index rebuild (CHG-48222) is not the cause of the 20+ second delays or failures, as its latency increase was only ~280 ms and orchestrator's timeout to knowledge-index is 800 ms with 0 retries.
The 6% conversation failure rate is entirely accounted for by queries that exhausted all 3 retry attempts against llm-provider and received fallback messages.

assumptions.statement: llm-provider calculates token quotas using a sliding multi-minute window or applied an unannounced tier/quota policy enforcement at 05:50 UTC.
No internal service configuration was reloaded dynamically without deployment or change records.
assistant-orchestrator evaluates retries on individual requests without shared token-bucket rate smoothing or circuit breaking.

The root cause is thus definitively established as upstream llm-provider token rate limiting compounded by orchestrator retry delays.
